question:
With reference to Article 142 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. It empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in a cause or matter pending before it.
2. The High Courts may exercise an identical power while deciding petitions under Article 226.
3. The Supreme Court has held that this power cannot be exercised in a manner inconsistent with the substantive provisions of a statute.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 restates Article 142(1). Statement 2 is wrong: Article 142 is exclusive to the Supreme Court, and in Anil Kumar Jain v. Maya Jain the Court held that High Courts cannot exercise an equivalent power under Article 226. Statement 3 reflects Prem Chand Garg (1963) and SCBA v. Union of India (1998). On 1 September 2026 a Bench of CJI Surya Kant, J. Joymalya Bagchi and J. V. Mohana used Article 142 to quash all FIRs registered between 20 and 25 July 2026 over the NEET-UG paper-leak protests and to bar fresh FIRs on the same events.
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Judiciary — powers and jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
micro_topic: Article 142 and 'complete justice'; Supreme Court order of 1 September 2026 quashing nationwide NEET-UG protest FIRs; Article 142(1) and 142(2); Union Carbide (1991) and Delhi Judicial Service Association (1991) as enabling authority; Prem Chand Garg (1963) and SCBA v. UoI (1998) as limits; Anil Kumar Jain v. Maya Jain on non-availability to High Courts

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Status of Coral Reefs of the World' report released in August 2026:
1. It was released by the Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network, which operates under the International Coral Reef Initiative.
2. It records that the interval between major reef disturbance events has lengthened from about five years to about a decade.
3. It reports the sharpest single-year relative fall in global hard coral cover between 2023 and 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: GCRMN operates under the International Coral Reef Initiative (1994) with UNEP support and released the report on 31 August 2026, based on 21.1 million observations from 36,886 sites in 124 countries. Statement 2 inverts the central finding: the disturbance interval has shortened from roughly once a decade to every 4-6 years. Statement 3 is correct — global hard coral cover fell 8.9% in relative terms between 2023 and 2024, the sharpest single-year contraction on record, taking cover to 25.8%.
subject: Environment
theme: Marine ecosystems and climate change impacts
micro_topic: GCRMN 'Status of Coral Reefs of the World', released 31 August 2026; 21.1 million observations from 36,886 sites in 124 countries; ~9.5% net decline against the 1980-2009 baseline; 8.9% relative fall 2023-24; cover 25.8% in 2024; disturbance interval down from ~10 years to 4-6 years; four global bleaching events 1998-99, 2010-11, 2016-17, 2023-25; ROPME Sea Area -50% (2020-24); GCRMN under ICRI with UNEP support

question:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, launched in August 2026, was recently in the news. Which of the following statements about it is/are correct?
1. It carries a primary mirror of the same diameter as that of the Hubble Space Telescope.
2. It is placed in a low Earth orbit to allow servicing missions.
3. It uses gravitational microlensing as one of its techniques for detecting exoplanets.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: Roman, launched on 30 August 2026 on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center, carries a 2.4 m primary mirror — the same diameter as Hubble's — but a 300-megapixel near-infrared Wide Field Instrument giving a field of view about 100 times larger. Statement 2 is wrong: Roman is bound for a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L2, roughly 1.5 million km away, far beyond servicing range; Hubble, in low Earth orbit, was the serviceable telescope. Microlensing is one of Roman's two principal exoplanet techniques, alongside its Coronagraph Instrument.
subject: Science & Technology
micro_topic: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched 30 August 2026, 7:26 a.m. EDT, Falcon Heavy from LC-39A Kennedy Space Center; formerly WFIRST; named for NASA's first Chief of Astronomy; 2.4 m mirror, 300-megapixel Wide Field Instrument, ~100x Hubble field of view; Coronagraph Instrument with >10^9 starlight suppression; Sun-Earth L2 halo orbit; dark energy, dark matter and exoplanet census via gravitational microlensing; contrast with Hubble (LEO), JWST (L2, 6.5 m), Chandra (X-ray) and AstroSat

question: Larak Island, seen in the news recently, is best described as:
options: (a) An Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, lying east of Qeshm Island and off the coast of Bandar Abbas
(b) An Omani island at the mouth of the Gulf of Aden, forming part of the Musandam governorate
(c) A disputed island in the Red Sea administered by Saudi Arabia and claimed by Egypt
(d) An Emirati island in the Persian Gulf hosting the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline terminus
explanation: Larak is an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, immediately east of Qeshm and south of Hormuz Island, geologically a salt diapir (salt plug formed by halokinesis) rising to about 138 m. US forces struck IRGC rocket launchers there on 30 August 2026 after detecting preparations to fire rockets carrying naval sea mines into the Strait. Option (b) misplaces it at the Gulf of Aden; (c) describes the Tiran and Sanafir dispute; (d) is fabricated — the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline terminates on the UAE's Gulf of Oman coast, not on an island.
subject: Geography
theme: Places in news — maritime chokepoints of West Asia
micro_topic: Larak Island, Strait of Hormuz, off Bandar Abbas, east of Qeshm and south of Hormuz Island; salt diapir formed by halokinesis, elevation ~138 m; Laraki dialect of Kumzari; 16th-century Portuguese fortifications; US strike on IRGC rocket launchers 30 August 2026; Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, narrowest width ~21 nautical miles, Iran to the north and Oman's Musandam exclave and the UAE to the south; bypass pipelines Petroline (Yanbu) and Habshan-Fujairah

question: Rani Avantibai Lodhi, whose statue was unveiled in Lucknow in August 2026, is associated with which one of the following?
options: (a) The Gond kingdom of Garha-Katanga in the sixteenth century
(b) The estate of Ramgarh in the Mahakoshal region during the Revolt of 1857
(c) The Bhil uprisings of the Khandesh region in the 1820s
(d) The Santhal Hool of 1855-56 in the Rajmahal Hills
explanation: Maharani Avantibai Lodhi (16 August 1831 - 20 March 1858) was queen-regent of Ramgarh in the Mahakoshal region, in present-day Dindori and Mandla districts of Madhya Pradesh. The British placed the estate under the Court of Wards because her heirs were minors — not under the Doctrine of Lapse — and she expelled the administrators, allied with the Gond ruler Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla, defeated Deputy Commissioner Waddington at the Battle of Kheri and chose martyrdom at Sukhi-Talaiya. Option (a) describes Rani Durgavati, the sixteenth-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga — the standard confusion this question tests. Rajnath Singh unveiled her statue in Lucknow on 30 August 2026.
subject: Modern History
theme: Revolt of 1857 — regional centres and leaders
micro_topic: Rani Avantibai Lodhi (1831-1858), queen-regent of Ramgarh, Mahakoshal (Dindori/Mandla, MP), born at Mankedi, Seoni; Court of Wards and sarbarahkars distinguished from the Doctrine of Lapse; alliance with Gond ruler Raja Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla; the bangle appeal; Battle of Kheri near Mandla; guerrilla operations from Devhargarh; martyrdom 20 March 1858 at Sukhi-Talaiya; statue unveiled in Lucknow 30 August 2026 by Rajnath Singh with Yogi Adityanath

question:
With reference to the Lagrange points of the Sun-Earth system, consider the following statements:
1. Of the five Lagrange points, L4 and L5 are the stable ones.
2. L2 lies on the side of the Earth away from the Sun.
3. India's Aditya-L1 mission was placed in a halo orbit around L2.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: L4 and L5 (the Trojan points) are the stable Lagrange points; L1, L2 and L3 are unstable and require station-keeping. L2 lies on the anti-Sun side of the Earth, about 1.5 million km away, which is why JWST and the newly launched Roman Space Telescope use it — Sun, Earth and Moon stay in one direction, allowing a single sunshield and a thermally stable environment. Statement 3 is wrong: Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit around L1, the point between the Sun and the Earth, chosen for continuous unobstructed solar observation.
subject: Science & Technology
micro_topic: Lagrange points L1-L5 of the Sun-Earth system; L1, L2, L3 unstable and L4, L5 stable (Trojan points); L1 for continuous solar observation (Aditya-L1, September 2023) versus L2 for thermally stable deep-space observatories (JWST, Roman); L2 at ~1.5 million km on the anti-Sun side; station-keeping requirement for halo orbits

question:
With reference to the Revolt of 1857, consider the following pairs:
Centre of revolt : Leader
1. Jagdishpur : Kunwar Singh
2. Faizabad : Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
3. Sambalpur : Khan Bahadur Khan
4. Garha-Mandla : Shankar Shah
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched — Kunwar Singh, the octogenarian zamindar of the Ujjainiya Parmar clan, led the revolt at Jagdishpur in Bhojpur, Bihar; Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah led it at Faizabad; and the Gond ruler Shankar Shah led it at Garha-Mandla, being blown from a cannon at Jabalpur in September 1857 along with his son Raghunath Shah. Pair 3 is wrong: Sambalpur was led by Surendra Sai, while Khan Bahadur Khan led the revolt at Bareilly.
subject: Modern History
theme: Revolt of 1857 — storm centres and leadership
micro_topic: Centre-and-leader pairings of 1857: Delhi (Bahadur Shah II / Bakht Khan), Kanpur (Nana Saheb / Tantia Tope), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Bareilly (Khan Bahadur Khan), Jagdishpur (Kunwar Singh), Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah), Allahabad (Liaquat Ali), Sambalpur (Surendra Sai), Garha-Mandla (Shankar Shah), Ramgarh (Avantibai Lodhi), Assam (Kandarpeshwar Singha); links to UPSC Prelims 2005 question on Kunwar Singh and Jagdishpur
